alignments.note: No article morpheme stands in the title, so the supplied *the* joins the nominal expression it determines (rule 15).
Impersonal participle with the subject pronoun the ASV supplies for it (rule 17).
Suffix takes the pronoun realizing it (rule 18).

Corrected from the accepted alignment, which put *art* on the explicit subject pronoun. Rule 20 names `אַתְּ` among the subject pronouns that take only their own English while the construction-supplied copula joins the predicate, and `בַּת מִי אַתְּ` → *Whose daughter art thou* is that rule's own example of the copula going to the predicate noun. The predicate here is the participle `אֹכֶלֶת`, so it takes *art* together with its own *devourer* and the indefinite *a* rule 15 gives the nominal expression; the unit is discontinuous around the supplied *land* under rule 25.
The rectum of the construct participle takes *of men* (rule 19).

Explicit subject pronoun takes only its own *Thou* (rule 20). The copula stands beside it in the English word order but belongs to the written predicate, which is what rule 20 directs be read from the Hebrew clause rather than from that order.

The italic *land* is a lexical noun the ASV supplies where no source nominal stands; `אָתְּ` is already realized by *Thou*, so rule 18's demonstrative-plus-supplied-noun clause does not reach it and rule 17 leaves the supplied subject noun `added`.
Predicate participle with the indefinite article that belongs to it (rule 15).
Rectum of the construct participle takes *of ... nation* (rule 19); the qere singular is what the projection carries (rule 9).
`הָיִית` takes the auxiliary and copula the ASV writes for it.

review_notes: Corrected one placement: rule 20 puts the construction-supplied *art* on the written predicate `אֹכֶלֶת`, not on the explicit subject pronoun `אָתְּ`, which that rule names outright and which takes only its own *Thou*. The accepted alignment's reason — that the ASV writes *Thou land art* — is the English word order rule 20 expressly declines to read the clause by.
Unit v002 was decided to the qere, giving a singular `גּוֹיֵךְ` that the ASV's *thy nation* matches; the marginal *nations* is the other reading and is not what the projection carries.
The italic *land* stays `added`: the pronoun already has its English pronoun, so no morpheme licenses the supplied noun.
